name: Obadiah
interpretive_note: Not to be confused with the prophet Obadiah, author of the book bearing that name, who lived at a different time and appears in a separate entry.
source_summary: King Ahab's God-fearing palace steward, who secretly hid and fed a hundred of the LORD's prophets during Jezebel's persecution while still serving in Ahab's court.
family_friendly_summary: Obadiah worked as the palace manager for King Ahab, one of Israel's most wicked kings. This must have been a difficult position, because Ahab's wife Jezebel was working hard to kill off God's true prophets. But Obadiah secretly rescued a hundred prophets, hiding fifty of them at a time in two caves and providing them with food and water at his own risk. Later, Obadiah was the one Ahab sent out to search the land for water and grass during a severe drought, and it was during that search that Obadiah unexpectedly met the prophet Elijah, whom Ahab had been hunting for years. Obadiah's story shows that it's possible to remain faithful to God even while serving in a difficult, compromised environment.
adult_story: Obadiah served as steward over Ahab's household, a position of real trust and authority in the royal court, and Scripture specifically notes he "feared the LORD greatly" (1 Kings 18:3). During Jezebel's campaign to exterminate the LORD's prophets, Obadiah secretly took a hundred of them, hid fifty at a time in two caves, and supplied them with bread and water at significant personal risk had Jezebel discovered it (18:4, 13). During the severe drought Elijah had pronounced, Ahab sent Obadiah out across the land searching for any remaining grass to keep the royal horses and mules alive, and along the way Obadiah unexpectedly encountered Elijah himself, whom Ahab had been hunting for three years (18:5-10). Obadiah was afraid to deliver word to Ahab that Elijah wished to meet him, worried the prophet might vanish again by the Spirit and leave Obadiah to bear Ahab's wrath for the false report, but Elijah swore he would keep his word, and Obadiah delivered the message that set up the Mount Carmel showdown (18:11-16). Obadiah's short account is a rare and valuable picture of quiet, costly faithfulness maintained inside a genuinely compromised and dangerous position -- proof that not everyone close to Ahab's throne had bowed the knee to Baal.

devotionals: Obadiah served in a wicked king's court yet secretly risked everything to save a hundred of God's prophets. May we stay faithful to Jesus, even in compromised places.
Obadiah feared the LORD greatly even surrounded by Baal worship at every turn. Jesus keeps His own faithful even in the hardest environments.
